Does giving an AI agent the freedom to re-search actually improve retrieval across 298 test questions?

A recent evaluation compared plain search against Agentic RAG, where an AI agent searched again whenever it chose. The agent found some papers that plain search missed, but it also lost papers that plain search had found. Ultimately, the performance gain was too small to trust.

Why it matters: Adding complexity to retrieval pipelines does not automatically guarantee better results than a plain search baseline.
